quiz.q: How did large landowners in India primarily evade land ceiling legislation to retain their holdings?
options: By transferring land through benami transactions and formally dividing joint family holdings.
By successfully challenging the Ninth Schedule in the Supreme Court to nullify ceiling acts.
By converting their agricultural land into cooperative farming societies managed by landless tillers.
By voluntarily surrendering their surplus land to obtain industrial compensation from the state.
quiz.why: Landlords exploited legal loopholes by transferring plots under fictitious benami names and dividing joint families to bypass ceilings.

quiz.q: According to Gunnar Myrdal, why did India fail to achieve meaningful land redistribution under Jawaharlal Nehru?
options: The peasantry organized radical nationwide mobilizations that forced the state to retreat from reforms.
India functioned as a soft state lacking administrative will and capacity to confront propertied elites.
The judicial repeal of the Ninth Schedule prevented Parliament from passing progressive agrarian legislation.
Rapid post-colonial industrial growth rendered rural land redistribution irrelevant to economic development.
quiz.why: Myrdal characterized India as a soft state that enacted progressive social laws but lacked the political and administrative will to enforce them.

quiz.q: How did economist V.K.R.V. Rao evaluate the socio-economic consequences of the Green Revolution in India?
options: It quadrupled total farm income and improved the bargaining strength of agricultural labourers.
It completely eliminated tenant eviction by securing equitable distribution of modern high-yielding inputs.
It widened the rich-poor divide and increased indebtedness among small farmers who lost land.
It ended rural disguised unemployment without causing inflation or displacing traditional farm workers.
quiz.why: V.K.R.V. Rao argued that the Green Revolution deepened inequality and forced small farmers into debt to buy expensive inputs, ultimately causing them to lose land.

quiz.q: What political transformation did Rudolph and Rudolph identify as a major outcome of the Green Revolution?
options: The complete decline of caste mobilization in favour of class-based peasant parties in northern India.
The rise of bullock capitalists as medium farmers who leveraged caste identity into regional political power.
The total centralization of agricultural policy making by foreign and indigenous bourgeois industrialists.
The immediate outbreak of widespread communist counter-revolutions across all major agricultural states.
quiz.why: Rudolph and Rudolph argued that the Green Revolution created an economically self-sufficient stratum of medium farmers ('bullock capitalists') who reshaped regional politics through caste mobilization.
